description: The Hot Serial Cereal experiment at Maricopa, Arizona, tests wheat under contrasting planting dates and infrared warming. Twenty-seven treatment combinations with three replicates span air temperatures from minus two to 42 degrees Celsius. The published measurements cover management, soils, weather, crop physiology, growth, yield and quality. Harvard Dataverse’s resource API confirms a RAR archive with CC0 rights for free reuse. The data can calibrate wheat temperature-response and agricultural-water simulations, and provide the experimental basis for related multi-model comparisons. A single cultivar and site provide limited evidence for all wheat-growing systems, and warming treatments do not reproduce every future climate change. No directly related catalogue record was identified.
name: Data on wheat response to a wide range of temperatures, as determined from the Hot Serial Cereal (HSC) Experiment
